options.text: Earth's pull on the stone is a non-contact force because it acts without the Earth touching the stone.
Earth's pull on the stone is a contact force because the stone will later land on the ground.
The hand's push on the eraser is a contact force because the hand touches the eraser.
Both forces are contact forces because both the stone and the eraser can move.

stem:
The diagram shows Earth's pull on a stone in the air and Krish's hand pushing an eraser across a desk while touching it.

Which claims correctly classify these forces? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Gravity acts without contact (non-contact). The hand push needs touch (contact). Later landing or mere motion does not reclassify the forces.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into Earth–stone pull and hand–eraser push.
